title: Judges Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 15.

questions.question: What did Samson bring when he visited his wife during the wheat harvest?
questions.correctAnswer: A kid
questions.explanation: Judges 15:1 states that Samson visited his wife with a kid during the wheat harvest.

questions.question: Why did Samson's father-in-law refuse to let him go into his wife?
options: He thought Samson hated his wife
He wanted to keep her for himself
Samson was not allowed to visit
questions.correctAnswer: He thought Samson hated his wife
questions.explanation: Judges 15:2 explains that her father thought Samson hated her, so he gave her to Samson's companion instead.

questions.question: What did Samson say about himself compared to the Philistines?
questions.correctAnswer: He is more blameless
questions.explanation: Judges 15:3 records Samson saying he shall be more blameless than the Philistines, even if he displeases them.

questions.question: How many foxes did Samson catch before setting them on fire?
questions.correctAnswer: Three hundred
questions.explanation: Judges 15:4 states Samson caught three hundred foxes to use in his plan.

questions.question: How did Samson arrange the foxes before setting them loose?
options: In a circle with firebrands in the middle
Tail to tail with a firebrand between two tails
In a line with firebrands at the front
questions.correctAnswer: Tail to tail with a firebrand between two tails
questions.explanation: Judges 15:4 describes Samson tying foxes tail to tail with firebrands placed between two tails.

questions.question: What did the foxes set on fire in the land of the Philistines?
options: The shocks, standing corn, vineyards, and olives
questions.correctAnswer: The shocks, standing corn, vineyards, and olives
questions.explanation: Judges 15:5 tells that the foxes set fire to the shocks, standing corn, vineyards, and olives of the Philistines.

questions.question: Who did the Philistines say was responsible for the burning?
options: Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite
questions.correctAnswer: Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite
questions.explanation: Judges 15:6 reveals the Philistines identified Samson, their son-in-law, as the culprit for the burning.

questions.question: What did the Philistines do to Samson's wife and her father?
questions.correctAnswer: They burned them with fire
questions.explanation: Judges 15:6 states the Philistines burned Samson's wife and her father with fire.

questions.question: What was Samson's response after the Philistines burned his wife and her father?
options: He said he would be avenged and then cease
He sought peace with the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: He said he would be avenged and then cease
questions.explanation: Judges 15:7 records Samson declaring he would be avenged of the Philistines and then stop.

questions.question: True or False: Samson visited his wife during the grape harvest.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 15:1 specifies the time as the wheat harvest, not grape harvest.

questions.question: True or False: Samson caught 300 foxes and used firebrands to burn the Philistines' crops.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 15:4-5 describe Samson catching 300 foxes, tying firebrands to their tails, and burning the Philistines' crops.

questions.question: True or False: The Philistines were unaware that Samson was responsible for the destruction of their fields.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 15:6 shows the Philistines identified Samson as the one who caused the destruction.

questions.question: True or False: Samson said that he would continue to seek revenge against the Philistines indefinitely.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 15:7 quotes Samson saying he will be avenged and then cease, not continue indefinitely.

questions.question: In Judges 15, which event happened first?
options: Samson visited his wife with a kid
The Philistines burned Samson's wife and her father
questions.correctAnswer: Samson visited his wife with a kid
questions.explanation: Judges 15:1 describes Samson visiting his wife first before the other events occurred.

questions.question: What reason did Samson's father-in-law give for giving Samson's wife to another man?
options: Samson was away for too long
questions.correctAnswer: He thought Samson hated her
questions.explanation: Judges 15:2 states the father thought Samson hated his wife, so he gave her to another man.

medium.title: Judges Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was Samson's response when the men of Judah confronted him about the Philistines ruling over them?
options: He said he had done nothing wrong
He said, 'As they did unto me, so have I done unto them'
He apologized and promised to stop
He asked them to join him against the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: He said, 'As they did unto me, so have I done unto them'
questions.explanation: Judges 15:11 records that when the men of Judah confronted Samson about the Philistines' rule, he responded, 'As they did unto me, so have I done unto them.' This shows his justification for his actions against the Philistines.

questions.question: Why did the men of Judah want to bind Samson and deliver him to the Philistines?
options: Because Samson had stolen from them
To stop him from fighting the Philistines
Because the Philistines wanted to punish Samson for his actions
Because Samson had insulted their elders
questions.correctAnswer: Because the Philistines wanted to punish Samson for his actions
questions.explanation: Judges 15:10 explains that the Philistines came to bind Samson in retaliation for what he had done to them, and the men of Judah intended to deliver him to the Philistines to avoid further conflict.

questions.question: How did Samson assure the men of Judah before allowing them to bind him?
options: He told them he would escape
He asked them to swear they would not kill him
He promised to stop fighting the Philistines
He warned them of God's judgment
questions.correctAnswer: He asked them to swear they would not kill him
questions.explanation: In Judges 15:12, Samson requested the men of Judah to swear that they would not kill him after binding him, showing his concern for his life even as he accepted being handed over.

questions.question: What happened to the cords binding Samson when the Spirit of the LORD came upon him at Lehi?
options: They tightened and held him fast
They became as flax burnt with fire and fell off
They were cut by a Philistine soldier
They were removed by the men of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: They became as flax burnt with fire and fell off
questions.explanation: Judges 15:14 states that when the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon Samson, the cords binding him became like burnt flax and his bands loosed from his hands, demonstrating God's power enabling his deliverance.

questions.question: What does Samson's action of slaying a thousand men with the jawbone of an ass teach about reliance on God's power?
options: God empowers the weak to overcome great foes
Weapons are the key to success
questions.correctAnswer: God empowers the weak to overcome great foes
questions.explanation: Judges 15:15-16 shows Samson using an unconventional weapon to slay many enemies, emphasizing that it was by the Spirit of the LORD coming upon him that he achieved this, teaching reliance on God rather than human might.

questions.question: What name did Samson give to the place where he cast away the jawbone, and what does it signify?
questions.correctAnswer: Ramathlehi, meaning 'Jawbone Height'
questions.explanation: Judges 15:17 records that after defeating the Philistines, Samson called the place Ramathlehi, linking the victory to the jawbone used, symbolizing God's deliverance through an unexpected means.

questions.question: How does Samson's prayer for water after the battle at Lehi demonstrate faith in God's provision?
options: He trusted God to provide refreshment after victory
He expected to find water without God’s help
He ignored his thirst and focused on battle
He doubted God's care for his needs
questions.correctAnswer: He trusted God to provide refreshment after victory
questions.explanation: Judges 15:18-19 shows Samson calling on the LORD in his thirst, acknowledging God's prior deliverance and trusting God would provide water, which God miraculously did, reinforcing faith in God’s care.

questions.question: What lesson about obedience and consequences can be learned from the men of Judah binding Samson to deliver him to the Philistines?
options: Disobedience to God’s calling leads to conflict with others
Obedience always leads to personal safety
Delivering others to enemies is always right
questions.correctAnswer: Disobedience to God’s calling leads to conflict with others
questions.explanation: Judges 15:11-13 illustrates the men of Judah opposing Samson despite his role against the Philistines, showing that failing to support God's appointed deliverer can lead to division and conflict.

questions.question: True or False: Samson lived in a cave called Etam after slaying the Philistines.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 15:8 states that Samson dwelt in the top of the rock Etam, not a cave, after his victory, showing a high place of refuge rather than a cave.

questions.question: True or False: The men of Judah intended to kill Samson when they bound him to hand him over to the Philistines.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 15:13 clarifies that the men of Judah said they would bind Samson and deliver him to the Philistines but would not kill him themselves, indicating they sought to avoid killing him.

questions.question: True or False: The Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon Samson when he was bound by cords, enabling him to break free.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 15:14 clearly states that when Samson was bound and brought to Lehi, the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, causing the cords to become like burnt flax and his bands to loosen.

questions.question: What does the Philistines' burning of Samson’s wife and her father reveal about the consequences of personal conflicts in this chapter?
options: It shows how personal disputes can escalate into violence
It was an act of mercy to end the conflict
It was unrelated to Samson’s actions
questions.correctAnswer: It shows how personal disputes can escalate into violence
questions.explanation: Judges 15:6 reveals that because Samson took his wife and gave her to his companion, the Philistines retaliated by burning her and her father, showing how personal issues led to violent escalation.

questions.question: How does Samson’s act of catching foxes and setting fire to the Philistines’ crops illustrate biblical principles of retribution and justice?
options: It teaches that revenge is always wrong
It shows a proportional response to offense
questions.correctAnswer: It shows a proportional response to offense
questions.explanation: Judges 15:4-5 describe Samson catching 300 foxes to burn the Philistine crops, reflecting a direct retaliation that parallels the offense, indicating a form of retributive justice in the narrative context.

questions.question: What encouragement can Christians learn about prayer from Samson’s experience of thirst and God providing water in Judges 15?
options: Prayer is unnecessary for physical needs
God listens and provides in times of desperation
Only spiritual needs should be prayed for
God never intervenes in earthly matters
questions.correctAnswer: God listens and provides in times of desperation
questions.explanation: Judges 15:18-19 shows Samson praying for water and God providing miraculously, teaching believers that God hears and answers prayers, especially in dire circumstances.

questions.question: Based on Judges 15, how should a believer respond when facing overwhelming opposition like Samson did?
options: Rely on their own strength to overcome
Seek God's help and trust His deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: Seek God's help and trust His deliverance
questions.explanation: Judges 15:14-15 and 18-19 demonstrate Samson relying on the Spirit of the LORD and seeking God's help in battle and need, teaching believers to depend on God's power and deliverance amid opposition.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 15.

questions.question: What object did Samson use to slay a thousand men?
options: A new jawbone of an ass
questions.correctAnswer: A new jawbone of an ass
questions.explanation: Judges 15:15 states that Samson found a new jawbone of an ass, took it, and slew a thousand men therewith, making it the weapon he used.

questions.question: What name did Samson give to the place after he killed a thousand men with the jawbone?
questions.correctAnswer: Ramathlehi
questions.explanation: Judges 15:17 explains that after speaking, Samson cast away the jawbone and called that place Ramathlehi, meaning 'the hill of the jawbone.'

questions.question: What did Samson do when he was extremely thirsty after the battle?
options: He drank from a nearby river
He called on the LORD for help
He asked the Philistines for water
questions.correctAnswer: He called on the LORD for help
questions.explanation: Judges 15:18 shows Samson calling on the LORD because he was sore athirst and feared dying of thirst and falling into the hands of the uncircumcised.

questions.question: How did God provide water to Samson after he was thirsty?
options: Water came from a spring in the ground
God clave an hollow place in the jawbone, and water came out
questions.correctAnswer: God clave an hollow place in the jawbone, and water came out
questions.explanation: Judges 15:19 states that God cleaved a hollow place in the jawbone, and water came out, which Samson drank and revived.

questions.question: For how many years did Samson judge Israel during the days of the Philistines?
questions.correctAnswer: 20 years
questions.explanation: Judges 15:20 clearly records that Samson judged Israel in the days of the Philistines for twenty years.

questions.question: What was the reason Samson gave for his actions against the Philistines when confronted by the men of Judah?
options: As they did unto me, so have I done unto them
He sought revenge for his wife
questions.correctAnswer: As they did unto me, so have I done unto them
questions.explanation: Judges 15:11 records Samson's reply to the men of Judah that he has done to the Philistines as they did to him.

questions.question: What was the Philistines' response after Samson burned their crops with firebrands tied to foxes?
options: They blamed the men of Judah
They burnt Samson's wife and her father with fire
questions.correctAnswer: They burnt Samson's wife and her father with fire
questions.explanation: Judges 15:6 says the Philistines burnt Samson's wife and her father with fire in retaliation for the destruction.

questions.question: What literary device is exemplified by the naming of the place Ramathlehi after Samson's victory?
questions.correctAnswer: Eponymous naming
questions.explanation: Judges 15:17 uses eponymous naming, where a place is named after an event or person, here 'Ramathlehi' after the jawbone victory.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'clave' in Judges 15:19, meaning 'to split or cleave,' signifies what about God's intervention?
questions.correctAnswer: A violent or forceful act
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root 'פָּרַץ' (paratz), translated 'clave', implies a forceful splitting, indicating God's powerful intervention providing water.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of God providing water miraculously to satisfy thirst, as seen in Judges 15:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 17:6
questions.explanation: In Exodus 17:6, God commands Moses to strike the rock, bringing forth water for the Israelites, paralleling God's provision of water to Samson in Judges 15:19.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage can be connected to Samson's call on the LORD for deliverance as seen in Judges 15:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 11:32
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:32 references Samson among the heroes of faith who called upon God for deliverance, connecting to Judges 15:18 where Samson calls on the LORD.

questions.question: What cultural significance did the act of binding Samson with two new cords have in the ancient Near Eastern context as seen in Judges 15:13?
options: It represented a binding oath and captivity
It was a ritual for marriage
questions.correctAnswer: It represented a binding oath and captivity
questions.explanation: In Judges 15:13, binding Samson with two new cords signified a serious captivity meant to restrain him, consistent with Near Eastern practices of binding prisoners securely.

questions.question: True or False: Samson was willing to cease his vengeance after avenging the burning of his wife and her father.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 15:7 quotes Samson saying, 'Though ye have done this, yet will I be avenged of you, and after that I will cease,' indicating his intent to stop after avenging.

questions.question: True or False: The men of Judah refused to hand Samson over to the Philistines after binding him with cords.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 15:13 states the men of Judah bound Samson and intended to deliver him into the Philistines' hand, not refusing but cooperating.

questions.question: Which passage in the Old Testament shares a thematic parallel with Samson's burning of the Philistine crops using foxes with firebrands (Judges 15:4-5)?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 9:18
questions.explanation: Isaiah 9:18 uses the imagery of firebrands among broom trees to describe destruction, paralleling Samson's use of burning foxes in Judges 15:4-5.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by Samson's act of burning the Philistines' crops with foxes and firebrands?
questions.correctAnswer: Divine judgment upon enemies
questions.explanation: Judges 15:4-5 shows Samson initiating destruction on the Philistines’ resources, representing a form of divine judgment against Israel’s oppressors, a recurring biblical theme of God using His instruments to punish wickedness (cf. Exodus 15:3).

questions.question: What does Samson’s thirst and God providing water from the jawbone signify about God's nature in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s provision and sustaining grace
questions.explanation: In Judges 15:18-19, Samson's desperate thirst and God’s miraculous provision of water illustrate God’s sustaining grace even during human weakness, affirming His care for His servants as also seen in Exodus 17:6.

questions.question: How does the narrative in Judges 15 emphasize the doctrine of human sinfulness and its consequences through Samson's interactions with his wife’s family and the Philistines?
options: Samson’s personal failures bring conflict and violence
God directly punishes Samson for his sins
The Philistines repent and reconcile with Israel
Peace is maintained despite human sin
questions.correctAnswer: Samson’s personal failures bring conflict and violence
questions.explanation: Judges 15:1-7 reveals that Samson’s failure to secure his wife and the ensuing retaliation by the Philistines escalate violence, highlighting the destructive consequences of human sinfulness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated by the Spirit of the LORD coming mightily upon Samson to empower him to break free from his bonds?
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence
questions.explanation: Judges 15:14 shows the Spirit of the LORD strengthening Samson supernaturally, displaying God's omnipotence to empower and deliver His chosen servant.

questions.question: What theological insight emerges when combining Samson’s killing of a thousand men with the jawbone (Judges 15:15-16) and his subsequent naming of the place Ramathlehi (Judges 15:17)?
options: God’s deliverance leads to memorializing His acts
The futility of violence as a solution
The inevitability of death for sinners
questions.correctAnswer: God’s deliverance leads to memorializing His acts
questions.explanation: Judges 15:15-17 shows Samson empowered by God to defeat enemies and then naming the place to commemorate God's deliverance, teaching how God’s acts of salvation are remembered and celebrated (cf. Exodus 17:15).

questions.question: What does the refusal of Samson’s father-in-law to allow him to visit his wife reveal about human relational sin and its disruption of God’s covenant purposes?
options: Human sin causes broken trust and relational betrayal
The Philistines honor Israelite marriage customs
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin causes broken trust and relational betrayal
questions.explanation: Judges 15:1-2 shows the father-in-law’s rejection of Samson, revealing human sin’s impact on covenant relationships and social trust, disrupting God's intended order for marriage and community.

questions.question: How does Judges 15:11-13 demonstrate the tension between human authority and divine empowerment in the story of Samson?
options: Human authorities seek to control Samson, but God empowers him beyond human constraints
Samson submits fully to human authority
The Philistines appoint Samson as their ruler
questions.correctAnswer: Human authorities seek to control Samson, but God empowers him beyond human constraints
questions.explanation: Verses 11-13 depict Judah men binding Samson to deliver him to the Philistines, yet God’s Spirit enables Samson to break free, illustrating divine empowerment surpassing human authority.

questions.question: What Christological foreshadowing is present in Samson’s deliverance of Israel in Judges 15:20?
options: Samson as a type of Christ delivering Israel from oppression
Samson as a priest offering sacrifices
Samson as a king reigning in righteousness
Samson as a prophet foretelling the Messiah
questions.correctAnswer: Samson as a type of Christ delivering Israel from oppression
questions.explanation: Judges 15:20 states Samson judged Israel for 20 years during Philistine oppression, foreshadowing Christ’s ultimate deliverance of His people from sin and enemies (cf. Luke 1:68).

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine justice and human retribution can be drawn from Judges 15:6 and Judges 15:8 regarding Samson’s response to the Philistines’ actions?
options: God’s justice often works through human agents to execute retribution
Human vengeance is condemned by God
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice often works through human agents to execute retribution
questions.explanation: Judges 15:6 records the Philistines’ violent retaliation, and 15:8 shows Samson’s severe counterattack, revealing the biblical pattern where God’s justice can be manifested through human actions in delivering retribution.

questions.question: What key doctrinal lesson regarding God’s providence is illustrated by God creating a hollow place in the jawbone to provide water for Samson (Judges 15:19)?
options: God providentially sustains His servants even in dire circumstances
God’s judgment is immediate and unrelenting
God requires human works for provision
God’s presence is hidden from His people
questions.correctAnswer: God providentially sustains His servants even in dire circumstances
questions.explanation: Judges 15:19 teaches that God miraculously provided water to Samson through the jawbone, emphasizing God’s providential care and sustenance in times of need (cf. Psalm 23:1-3).

questions.question: How does the conflict between the men of Judah and Samson (Judges 15:10-13) deepen our understanding of the doctrine of sanctification in the midst of a fallen world?
options: Sanctification involves tension between God’s calling and flawed human community
Sanctification depends solely on human effort
Sanctification is irrelevant to social relationships
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves tension between God’s calling and flawed human community
questions.explanation: Judges 15:10-13 shows Judah men opposing Samson despite his God-ordained mission, illustrating how sanctification occurs amidst human failure and conflict within the community of faith.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the violence and revenge in Judges 15 demonstrate an immoral God. What does Judges 15:7-8 actually teach about God's justice and judgment?
options: God’s justice includes righteous judgment executed through His chosen agents
God condones all human violence without distinction
God is indifferent to human suffering
God’s law forbids all forms of retribution
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice includes righteous judgment executed through His chosen agents
questions.explanation: Judges 15:7-8 shows Samson’s vow to be avenged and his subsequent defeat of the Philistines, illustrating that God enacts justice through His instruments against oppressors, consistent with divine righteousness (cf. Romans 12:19).

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed by His spirit coming mightily upon Samson at the moment of his deliverance from bondage?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s empowering grace
questions.explanation: Judges 15:14 states the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon Samson enabling him to break free, showcasing God's empowering grace that enables His servants beyond their natural strength.

questions.question: How does the narrative in Judges 15 demonstrate the doctrine of God’s faithfulness despite human weakness, particularly in Samson’s continued leadership over Israel?
options: God sustains His purposes through imperfect leaders
God only works through sinless individuals
God abandons Israel due to Samson’s failures
God’s promises are conditional on perfect obedience
questions.correctAnswer: God sustains His purposes through imperfect leaders
questions.explanation: Judges 15:20 reports Samson judged Israel 20 years despite his flaws, showing God’s faithfulness in accomplishing His redemptive purposes through imperfect human instruments (cf. 1 Corinthians 1:27-29).

questions.question: What does the dialogue between Samson and the men of Judah (Judges 15:11) reveal about the nature of Israel's subjugation under the Philistines and the role of divine deliverance?
options: Israel’s oppression under Philistine rule highlights the need for God’s deliverance through His chosen judge
Israel was free and prosperous under Philistine rule
The men of Judah fully supported Samson’s actions
Philistine rule was divinely ordained without hope of deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: Israel’s oppression under Philistine rule highlights the need for God’s deliverance through His chosen judge
questions.explanation: Judges 15:11 underscores Philistine dominance over Judah and Samson’s retaliatory acts as part of God’s provision of deliverance, emphasizing the ongoing struggle against oppression in Israel’s history.
